body.notes: Re-derived every part independently. (1) E[V]=1; |D|^0.5=(D^2)^(1/4) so H=E[V^(1/4)]; V^(1/4)<=1+V gives integrability; E[g(V)]=(3+1)/4-H=1-H. (2) E=2H^p-1=2(1-E[g(V)])^p-1; p=log0.5/log(2*3^-0.75)=5.29880>0 and H in (0,1] (H7, Jensen step rechecked), so E strictly decreases in E[g(V)]. (3) With finite fourth moment E[V^2]=kappa, so E[(V-1)^2]=kappa-1=excess kurtosis+2. (4) g'=(1-v^(-3/4))/4, g''=(3/16)v^(-7/4)>0 on v>0, g continuous at 0, hence strictly convex on [0,inf); g(1)=g'(1)=0 so g>0 for v!=1; g''(1)=3/16, g'''(1)=-21/64 bounded near 1, so g=(3/32)(v-1)^2+O(|v-1|^3); g(0)=3/4; g-v/4=3/4-v^(1/4)=O(v^(1/4)). (5) Scaled comparison: (32/3)g''(1)=2=second derivative of (v-1)^2, values and first derivatives both 0 at 1, so (32/3)g=(v-1)^2+O(|v-1|^3); (32/3)g(0)=8=8*(0-1)^2; (32/3)g(v)=8v/3+8-(32/3)v^(1/4). Numeric checks (mpmath): derivatives at 1 are 0, 0.1875, -0.328125; ((32/3)g(1+h)-h^2)/h^3 tends to about -0.583 (=-7/12) from both sides, confirming a third-order remainder; (32/3)g(v)/v tends to 8/3; for the exponential, quadrature of E[g(V)] equals 1-H=0.2120548 to 30 digits. Nothing wrong or missing. One wording remark, not an error: 'linear in V' far out holds to leading order (8v/3 plus a constant and a v^(1/4) term), i.e. growth of order v against v^2, which is what the H20 statement g=v/4+O(v^(1/4)) says exactly. The sentence that all three 'measure how far V spreads from 1' is an interpretation supported by (1)-(4) (both losses non-negative, zero only at v=1), not a separate theorem.

Closed forms match distributions.md: H16 exponential case R=sqrt(pi)/(2e), I=(2e-sqrt(pi)erfi(1))/(2e) at lambda=1 (sigma=1), sum =1-sqrt(pi)(erfi(1)-1)/(2e); H14 at nu=5 gives Gamma(0.75)Gamma(2.25)3^0.25/(sqrt(pi)Gamma(2.5)) since (nu-0.5)/2=2.25, nu-2=3, nu/2=2.5; H12 gives sqrt(pi)/2*2^-0.25. I re-derived these (Laplace: Gamma(1.5)b^0.5 over (2b^2)^0.25; t: E|T|^0.5 by the normal/chi-square ratio; exponential: antiderivative of x^2 e^(x^2) checked by differentiation) and verified each against direct quadrature of E|y-mean|^0.5/sigma^0.5 in mpmath to 30 digits: H=0.7879451592 (R=0.3260246661, I=0.4619204931), 0.7755040493, 0.7452250447. Excess kurtosis: exponential central mu4=9, sigma^2=1, so 6; t5 sigma^2=5/3, mu4=3*25/(3*1)=25, kurtosis 9, excess 6/(nu-4)=6; Laplace mu4=24b^4, sigma^4=4b^4, excess 3; all confirmed by quadrature. p=log0.5/log(2*3^-0.75)=5.2988028. E=2H^p-1 = -0.4343046, -0.4800546, -0.5789765, rounding to -0.434, -0.480, -0.579 as stated; no value is near a rounding boundary. Orderings: p>0 so E increases with H, and 0.7879>0.7755>0.7452; hence exponential and t5 have equal excess kurtosis 6 but different Extremity, and Laplace has lower excess kurtosis (3<6) yet lower Extremity than both, whereas if the two ordered alike a less kurtotic law would not be the most extreme in the same direction as... put plainly: kurtosis ties one pair that Extremity separates, so the orderings are not the same. Statement as worded follows. Nothing wrong or missing. Remark: 'do not order alike' is established by the tie-versus-strict-difference pair and by Laplace versus t5/exponential only if lower Extremity is read as heavier tails (lower kurtosis but 'more extreme'); under that reading it is a genuine reversal, and the proof text says so.
